data.one_liner: A pool of long‑living Dart isolates for running jobs or hosting objects off the main isolate.
data.what_it_does: The package creates and keeps active isolates ready to receive requests. It lets you schedule one‑off jobs like compute() but reuses isolates, and also host persistent objects accessed via proxies. Results are returned to the main isolate asynchronously.
use_when: You need to run heavy CPU‑bound tasks frequently without the overhead of spawning a new isolate each time
You want to keep stateful objects alive in isolates and communicate with them via RPC‑style calls
avoid_when: A single occasional compute() call is enough
You target web where isolates are not supported
You need UI‑related functionality or platform channels
strengths: Reuses isolates for better performance on repeated tasks
Supports persistent isolate instances with proxy communication
Pure Dart, no native setup required
weaknesses: Works only on platforms that support Dart isolates (no web)
Debugging cross‑isolate communication can be tricky
No built‑in serialization helpers, you must ensure data is isolate‑safe
